title: The Charge of Makkah • The Seat of Judgement • The Market and the Bayt al-Mal • Dhimmis, Workers and Subordinates • A Few More Commonly Circulated Narrations • Final Word

blocks.1: At Ji‘ranah itself the Prophet {{1}} put on ihram. Coming to Makkah he performed ‘umrah. Anas (RA) said,
blocks.3: The Prophet {{1}} performed four ‘umrahs, all in Dhu al-Qa‘dah; the ‘umrah of Hudaybiyah, the ‘umrah of the next year, the ‘umrah from Ji‘ranah where he had distributed the spoils of Hunayn, and the ‘umrah with Hajj.{{2}}
blocks.4: After completing it the Prophet {{1}} appointed ‘Attab ibn Usayd (RA) as governor of Makkah. Then he set out toward Madinah. On the twenty-fourth of Dhu al-Qa‘dah of the eighth year of Hijrah, he entered that long-familiar Madinah.{{2}}
blocks.5: The city that for twenty years had struck him, that city came into his hand, and he handed its charge to someone like ‘Attab, who was still new in Islam. But how the administration of Makkah should be, the principles of it the Prophet {{1}} told with his own mouth. If you ask for a post, not the post. Abu Musa al-Ash‘ari (RA) says, I and two of my people went to the Prophet {{2}}. One of them said, make us governors. The other said the same. The Prophet {{3}} said,
blocks.7: By Allah, we do not appoint to this work anyone who has asked for it, or who has coveted it.{{1}}
blocks.8: Abu Musa himself had not asked for that work, so he was the one sent to Yemen. He gave Mu‘adh ibn Jabal as his companion, and told them,
blocks.10: Make things easy, do not make them hard. Give good news, do not drive people away. Work in agreement, do not differ.{{1}}
blocks.11: One to whom a post is service does not run after posts. One to whom a post is power asks for posts the most. And the one who gets a post must remember first of all: make it easy, do not drive away, work in harmony. A man from Egypt came to ‘A’ishah (RA). ‘A’ishah asked, how has your ruler behaved with you? The man said, no complaint. If someone’s camel died he gave a camel, if a slave died a slave, if expenses were needed he gave expenses. ‘A’ishah (RA) then said, then listen, I heard the Messenger of Allah {{1}} say in this very house of mine,
blocks.13: O Allah, whoever is given charge of any matter of my ummah and is harsh with them, be harsh with him. And whoever is given charge of any matter of my ummah and is gentle with them, be gentle with him.{{1}}
blocks.14: And Ma‘qil ibn Yasar (RA), on his deathbed, said to the governor ‘Ubaydullah ibn Ziyad, if I had known I would live, I would not say this today. I heard the Messenger of Allah {{1}} say,
blocks.16: A servant to whom Allah gives charge of a people, who dies on the day he dies while cheating his subjects, Allah will forbid Paradise to him.{{1}}
blocks.17: The Qur’an has spoken of this very trust in this way,
blocks.19: (O Muslims!) Surely Allah commands you to deliver trusts to their rightful owners, and when you judge between people, to judge with justice. Be sure that what Allah counsels you is most excellent. Surely Allah hears everything, sees everything.{{1}}
blocks.20: A trust is not just money. A post is a trust, a decision is a trust, a person’s reliance is a trust. A sign of keeping a trust: at the time of delivering it to the rightful one, recognising him, remembering, not cheating someone and keeping it for oneself.
blocks.22: The Prophet {{1}} was at once commander, giver and judge. A few rules of sitting in the seat of judgement he told with his own mouth. Umm Salamah (RA) says, the Prophet {{2}} said,
blocks.24: You bring disputes to me. Perhaps some of you can arrange your argument better than another. If, hearing his words, I give him something of his brother’s right, then I have cut for him a piece of Hell; let him not take it.{{1}}
blocks.25: This is the word of a judge who is himself a prophet, upon whom revelation descends. Yet he admitted, I am a human; if someone states his argument beautifully I may give a ruling on his word. But even if I rule, the one who knows the right is not his, if he takes it he has taken a piece of fire. A judge’s ruling does not make the haram halal for anyone. Even if it is written on the court’s paper. Another rule, which Abu Bakrah (RA) wrote to his son who was in Sijistan. He had heard the Prophet {{1}} say,
blocks.27: Let no judge decide between two while he is angry.{{1}}
blocks.28: When angry a person forgets justice. A judge is only human; anger rises in him. So at the time of anger there is no seat for him. Today, those of us who take decisions about anyone, at home, in the office, in the madrasah, when there is anger let us pause for a while. A ruling given in anger never comes in the name of justice; it comes in the name of revenge.
blocks.29: The Market and the Bayt al-Mal
blocks.30: In today’s language, the Prophet {{1}} was then running a state. What the rules were for that state’s market, treasury and wealth, a few pictures are found in sahih narrations. The market. The Prophet {{2}} himself would go out to look at the market. One day, passing by a heap of foodgrain, he put in his hand and found it wet. He asked the owner, what is this? He said, it got wet in the rain, O Messenger of Allah. He said, why did you not put the wet part on top, so that people could see? Then he said,
blocks.32: Whoever cheats is not of me.{{1}}
blocks.33: In our market today dry goods are arranged on top and wet goods below. With the Prophet {{1}}, for this cheating not just a fine but a declaration: he is not of me. There is another matter he also told, which pulls at the very root of the market,
blocks.35: The Prophet {{1}} cursed the one who consumes riba, the one who gives riba, its writer and its two witnesses. He said, they are all the same.{{2}}
blocks.36: Those who write down the accounts of riba, they too. Those who are witnesses, they too. Four hands in one transaction. In the business of riba no one can think himself outside. The Bayt al-Mal. The wealth that comes into hand without war is called fay’. The rules for distributing it Allah Himself has fixed. The Qur’an says it in this way,
blocks.38: The wealth that Allah has granted His Messenger as ‘fay’’ from the people of other towns belongs to Allah, His Messenger, (the Messenger’s) relatives, the orphans, the needy and the wayfarers, so that it does not circulate only among the wealthy among you. Take what the Messenger gives you, and refrain from what he forbids you, and fear Allah. Surely Allah is severe in punishment.{{1}}
blocks.39: So that the wealth does not circulate only among the wealthy; this condition is the root formula of a state’s economy. A system in which wealth goes and accumulates in one place, in the Qur’an’s language that system is itself on the road to breakdown. And the one who was the guardian of that wealth, what was his own reckoning? ‘Uqbah ibn al-Harith (RA) says, one day after ‘Asr the Prophet {{1}} gave the salam and rose quickly, stepped over people’s necks and went to his wife’s room. The people were alarmed. Coming out he said,
blocks.41: In my house some pieces of gold of the sadaqah were lying. I remembered. I did not want it to hold me back, so I ordered its distribution.{{1}}
blocks.42: A little gold of the sadaqah had remained in the house, and his restlessness over it. Today we leave office files, an organisation’s funds, a mosque’s donations lying in the house or the car; to him even one piece of gold was heavy to keep a night in the house. Waqf. Instead of hoarding wealth, the way of turning it into lasting good too the Prophet {{1}} showed. ‘Umar (RA) got a piece of land at Khaybar, than which he had never got more precious wealth. He asked the Prophet {{2}}, what shall I do? The Prophet {{3}} said,
blocks.44: If you wish, hold its principal and give its fruit as sadaqah.{{1}}
blocks.45: ‘Umar (RA) did just that. The land would not be sold, would not be given away, would not go by inheritance. Its fruit would go for the poor, relatives, freeing slaves, the way of Allah, wayfarers and guests. Whoever is in charge of looking after it may eat in a just manner, but may not accumulate wealth. The wealth I love most, by giving that to someone I have truly given. And I gave it in such a way that it will be of use forever. Waqf means this thought: even if I am gone, the thing I love will keep working for people.
blocks.47: About those who live under a covenant in a Muslim state, the Prophet {{1}} said,
blocks.49: Whoever kills a mu‘ahad will not smell the fragrance of Paradise, though the fragrance of Paradise can be smelled from a distance of forty years.{{1}}
blocks.50: To kill a non-Muslim citizen means being deprived even of the fragrance of Paradise. Yet that fragrance can be smelled from a distance of forty years. In this hadith the safety of the state’s weakest citizen is not just law but a condition of faith. And the right of the worker. Allah Himself has declared that He will be the plaintiff against three,
blocks.52: Allah says, on the Day of Resurrection I am the plaintiff against three: one who gave a promise in My name and then broke it; one who sold a free person and ate his price; and one who hired a labourer and extracted the full work from him, yet did not give his wages.{{1}}
blocks.53: Withholding wages is here in the same row as breaking a contract and selling people to eat their price. In today’s terms, not paying salary on time, cheating by working overtime, taking money in the name of giving a job, before these Allah Himself will stand on the Day of Resurrection. And the subordinate people, domestic workers, employees, slaves. Abu Dharr al-Ghifari (RA) once abused someone by taunting him about his mother. The Prophet {{1}} said, you are a man in whom there is Jahiliyyah. Then he said,
blocks.55: Your brothers are your subordinates. Allah has placed them under your hands. Whoever has his brother under his hand, let him feed him what he himself eats; clothe him in what he himself wears. And do not burden them with work that is beyond them. If you must burden them, help them.{{1}}
blocks.56: Abu Dharr dressed that slave like himself. People saw him at Rabadhah, one pair of clothes on his own body, one pair on the slave’s body too. By one word of the Prophet {{1}} a Companion changed the rule of his own house. Non-Muslim citizen, worker, subordinate. In the Prophet’s {{2}} state the rights of each of these are in the clear declarations of the Qur’an and hadith. Cheating in the market is forbidden; wealth shall circulate among all; if you ask for a post, not the post. The one who, seeing the hearts of the Ansar break, called them aside and explained, he too stands beside a heap of grain in the market. The same man. The heart that thinks about the Ansar’s hearts, that very heart thinks about a poor labourer’s wages too.
blocks.57: A Few More Commonly Circulated Narrations
blocks.58: About a few matters of this dars there are some more narrations that people tell or that are found in books. They too have been kept here. The chain and grade of each is given in the footnote. First, a narration on the rights of non-Muslims under a covenant. The sons of a group of Companions narrate from their fathers that the Messenger of Allah {{1}} said,
blocks.60: Beware! Whoever wrongs a non-Muslim under a covenant, reduces his right, burdens him beyond his capacity, or takes something from him without his satisfaction, I will be the plaintiff against him on the Day of Resurrection.{{1}}
blocks.61: Protecting those under covenant from all these forms of wrong is the Prophet’s {{1}} command. A narration on the worker’s wages is very commonly circulated, which is basically said in these words,
blocks.62: Give the labourer his wages before his sweat dries.{{1}}
blocks.63: Paying the worker’s right quickly, that is the idea here. There is a narration from Ibn Mas‘ud (RA) on the number of Companions at Hunayn. He says,
blocks.64: On the day of Hunayn we were with the Messenger of Allah {{1}}. The people drew back from him. And with him remained eighty Muhajirun and Ansar. We went back almost eighty paces, but we did not turn our backs.{{2}}
blocks.65: Whatever the number of those who were with the Prophet {{1}}, they did not turn their backs. There is a narration of Jabir ibn ‘Abdillah (RA) on the Prophet’s {{2}} du‘a for Thaqif beneath the fortress of Ta’if. The Companions said,
blocks.66: O Messenger of Allah, the arrows of Thaqif have burned us, curse them. He said, O Allah, guide Thaqif.{{1}}
blocks.67: Even for the enemy a prayer of guidance, this was his way. Finally a Sirah-based story, which is now found in many books. About Abu Bakrah Nufay‘ ibn al-Harith (RA),
blocks.68: When the Messenger of Allah {{1}} besieged the fortress of Ta’if, I came down from the fortress with the help of a pulley and came to the Messenger of Allah {{2}}. He asked, how did you come down? I said, by a pulley. He said, you are Abu Bakrah (the pulley-man).{{3}}
blocks.69: A slave came down from the fortress wall and came over to the side of Islam, and his very name became ‘Abu Bakrah’.
blocks.71: From Hunayn to Ji‘ranah, then Madinah, a few pictures of these few weeks stay in the mind. The new Muslims’ wish on seeing the jujube tree of Dhat Anwat, and the Prophet’s {{1}} correcting it at once. In the army of twelve thousand the words ‘today we will not lose’, and the rain of arrows of one dawn. A man on a white mule, I am the Prophet, no lie. People returning at ‘Abbas’s single call. Abu ‘Amir’s last words, tell the Prophet {{2}} to seek forgiveness for me. ‘We are returning’ for the Companions who stumbled beneath the fortress of Ta’if. On the lips not a curse but a prayer of guidance. Safwan in the tent at Ji‘ranah, whose dislike turned to love. The cloak caught on the thorn tree and a tuft of wool in the fist. The weeping of the Ansar, their beards wet. The delegation of Hawazin, the cloak spread for the milk-sister, Malik ibn ‘Awf’s return. Dhu al-Khuwaysirah’s ‘be just’. The charge of Makkah, the trust, the seat of judgement, the market, the Bayt al-Mal, the worker’s wages. We take decisions. In our own house, shop, office, madrasah, organisation. The reckoning of the decision is clear to us. But whose heart broke that day, we do not see. So take away one deed from today’s dars.
blocks.73: The Ansar had taken offence. The Prophet {{1}} did not brush it off, he called them aside and explained, and they wept. Today I will ask myself a question: by which of my decisions has someone’s heart been broken, and did I notice it, or did I assume it will be fine as time passes? Today the one whose heart my decision broke I will call aside and explain to, and I will listen to what they say too; I will not give up this habit from today.

Al-Rahiq al-Makhtum, p. 692 (Sirah-based part): put on ihram at Ji‘ranah itself, performed ‘umrah in Makkah, appointed ‘Attab ibn Usayd governor of Makkah and set out on the road to Madinah; entered Madinah on 24 Dhu al-Qa‘dah of 8 AH.
footnotes.1: Appointing ‘Attab ibn Usayd (RA) in charge of Makkah: al-Fiqh al-Sirah, Ghazali and al-Albani, p. 400 (al-Albani: hasan); al-Rahiq al-Makhtum, p. 679 (at setting out for Hunayn) and p. 692 (at returning to Madinah). The Sirah mentions leaving Mu‘adh ibn Jabal (RA) in Makkah to teach the Qur’an; this has not been said in this dars.
footnotes.2: Sahih al-Bukhari 7149 (Abu Musa al-Ash‘ari (RA): ‘I and two men of my people went to the Prophet {{1}}; one of them said, make us governors; the other said the same. He said, we do not appoint to this work one who asks for it or covets it’); Sahih Muslim 1733 (c, d), also Bukhari 2261.
footnotes.3: Sahih Muslim 1733 (a, b) (Abu Musa al-Ash‘ari (RA): the Prophet {{1}} gave this instruction when sending him and Mu‘adh (RA) to Yemen; sahih). ‘Tata‘a‘a’: follow one another. The details of sending Abu Musa and Mu‘adh to Yemen will come in Dars 24; here only the principle of leadership.
footnotes.4: Sahih Muslim 1828 (from ‘A’ishah (RA); via ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn Shimasah; sahih). Sahih al-Jami‘ 1312 (al-Albani: sahih). A man of Egypt told ‘A’ishah (RA), our amir behaved well with us; after the death of one’s camel he gave a camel, on a slave’s death a slave; then she told him this hadith.
footnotes.5: Sahih Muslim 142 (from Ma‘qil ibn Yasar al-Muzani (RA); sahih); Sahih al-Jami‘ 5740 (al-Albani: sahih). Ma‘qil (RA), on his deathbed, told ‘Ubaydullah ibn Ziyad the hadith and said, ‘had I known I would live I would not have told you.’
footnotes.6: Tawdih al-Qur’an, vol. 1, Surah al-Nisa’ 4:58, p. 256 (matched word for word by reading the printed page); note 81 on the next verse 59 (pp. 256–257): ‘those in authority’ according to most exegetes means the Muslim ruler; obedience to the ruler is obligatory in lawful matters, but not in orders against the Shari‘ah.
footnotes.7: Sahih al-Bukhari 2680 (from Umm Salamah (RA); sahih); Sahih Muslim 1713 too. ‘Alhan bi-hujjatihi’: can present his argument more cleverly.
footnotes.8: Sahih al-Bukhari 7158 (Abu Bakrah (RA) wrote to his son in Sijistan, ‘do not decide between two while angry’; sahih); Ahmad 20522 (Arna’ut: the chain is sahih, on the condition of the two Shaykhs).
footnotes.9: Sahih Muslim 102 (from Abu Hurayrah (RA); sahih); Jami‘ al-Tirmidhi 1315 (al-Albani: sahih). The incident: the Prophet {{1}}, passing by a heap of foodgrain, put in his hand and felt wetness; the owner said, it got wet in the rain; he said, ‘then why did you not put the wet part on top, so that people could see?’. ‘Man ghashsha fa-laysa minni’: in another narration ‘fa-laysa minna’.
footnotes.10: Sahih Muslim 1598 (from Jabir ibn ‘Abdillah (RA); sahih). Abu al-Zubayr Muhammad ibn Muslim, via Hushaym.
footnotes.11: Tawdih al-Qur’an, vol. 3, Surah al-Hashr 59:7, p. 515 (matched word for word by reading the printed page); note 5: ‘What the enemy side leaves behind without war is called fay’… In the next verse Allah the Exalted has given the list of those among whom the goods of fay’ must be distributed.’
footnotes.12: Sahih al-Bukhari 851 (from ‘Uqbah ibn al-Harith (RA); sahih): ‘I prayed ‘Asr behind the Prophet {{1}} in Madinah. Giving the salam he rose quickly, stepped over the necks of people toward one of his wives’ rooms; the people were alarmed. Coming out he said…’. ‘Tibr’: unrefined gold.
footnotes.13: Sahih al-Bukhari 2737 (from ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Umar (RA); sahih), Sahih Muslim 1632. The incident: ‘Umar (RA) got a piece of land at Khaybar, than which he had never got more valuable wealth; on the Prophet’s {{1}} advice he gave it as sadaqah in such a way that it would not be sold, given away or inherited; the fruit for the poor, relatives, freeing slaves, the way of Allah, wayfarers and guests; the supervisor may eat in a just manner. In Dars 16 there is the incident of the waqf of Mukhayriq’s orchard; this is ‘Umar’s waqf.
footnotes.14: Sahih al-Bukhari 3166 (from ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Amr ibn al-‘As (RA); sahih). ‘Mu‘ahad’: one with whom the Muslims have a covenant, a non-Muslim living under security. The rulings of jizyah and dhimmah and the system of collecting zakat are coming in Dars 24; here only the Prophet’s {{1}} general warning.
footnotes.15: Sahih al-Bukhari 2227 (from Abu Hurayrah (RA); sahih; hadith qudsi); also in Sahih al-Bukhari 2270. ‘A‘ta bi’: gave a promise or word in My name.
footnotes.16: Sahih al-Bukhari 30, 2545 (from Abu Dharr al-Ghifari (RA); sahih). The incident: when Abu Dharr (RA) abused a man by taunting him about his mother the Prophet {{1}} said, ‘you are a man in whom there is Jahiliyyah’. Abu Dharr (RA) then clothed his slave in clothes as costly as his own. ‘Khawal’: subordinate servants and slaves.
footnotes.17: Sunan Abi Dawud 3052 (sons of a group of Companions from their Companion fathers). Hasan, with disagreement: al-Albani, Sahih Abi Dawud 3052: sahih; Sahih al-Targhib 3006: hasan; Arna’ut, Takhrij Sunan Abi Dawud 3052: the chain is hasan, Takhrij Sharh al-Sunnah 11/180: the chain is strong; Ibn Hajar, Hidayat al-Ruwat 4/100: hasan (according to the principle of his introduction). On the other side Ibn al-Qattan, al-Wahm wa al-Iham 2/599: ‘a narration like this has been called sahih because the condition of these sons of Companions in the chain is unknown’; al-Mundhiri, Mukhtasar Sunan Abi Dawud 2/346: ‘fihi majhulun’ (the chain has unknown narrators). In this dars earlier Sahih al-Bukhari 3166 (killing a dhimmi) has come; in this narration further forms of wrong. Ruling: hasan; acceptable according to al-Albani and Arna’ut, the objection of Ibn al-Qattan and al-Mundhiri is about the unknown narrators of the chain.
footnotes.18: Give the labourer his wages before his sweat dries.
footnotes.19: We were with the Messenger of Allah {{1}} on the day of Hunayn, he said: the people turned away from him, and there stood firm with him eighty men of the Muhajirun and the Ansar, and we went back on our feet about eighty paces, and we did not turn our backs to them.
footnotes.20: They said: O Messenger of Allah! The arrows of Thaqif have burned us, so supplicate Allah against them. He said: O Allah, guide Thaqif.
footnotes.21: I came down to the Messenger of Allah {{1}} by a pulley, he said: how did you come down? I said: I came down by a pulley. He said: you are Abu Bakrah.

quiz.q: From Ji‘ranah, which act of worship did the Prophet ﷺ perform on coming to Makkah?
o: Hajj
‘Umrah
I‘tikaf
Qurbani

quiz.q: The Prophet ﷺ did not appoint a man who asked for a post; what is understood from this?
o: Those who seek posts are less educated
A post is service, so one does not run after it
It is forbidden to give posts to new Muslims
Appointing governors is the right of the Ansar

quiz.q: Someone says, ‘give me this post’; what is the Prophet’s ﷺ guidance?
o: Give it at once if asked
Give it if experienced
Give it if new
If you ask for a post, not the post

quiz.q: What does the instruction that a judge should not give a ruling while angry teach?
o: A judge never gets angry at all
When angry the witnesses change at once
A ruling in anger becomes revenge
Judgement can only be in the daytime

quiz.q: Before taking a decision about someone while in a bad mood, what should one do?
o: Pause and wait for the anger to subside
Quickly give the ruling
Have someone else give the ruling
Not announce the decision

quiz.q: Which Companion made a waqf of the land he got at Khaybar?
o: Abu Bakr (RA)
‘Uthman (RA)
‘Umar (RA)
‘Ali (RA)

quiz.q: In the market wet goods are arranged below and dry goods on top; what is the Prophet’s ﷺ statement?
o: Permissible since there is no riba
Whoever cheats is not of me
Selling goods is forbidden
Checking prices is not the government’s work

quiz.q: Which incident makes someone who leaves a mosque’s or an organisation’s donations lying in the house or car think?
o: ‘Umar’s waqf of the land at Khaybar
The cloak caught in the thorns at Ji‘ranah
Keeping the sadaqah gold in the house
The Ansar gathering in the leather tent

quiz.q: If one makes an employee work and withholds the wages, what will happen on the Day of Resurrection?
o: He will be forgiven
He will get middling reward
There will be only a fine
Allah Himself will be the plaintiff
